note: One entry per month: what the river, the trails and the town are doing. The build writes the current month; the browser re-picks by its own date. Keep each to what is true most years; the live gauge and the county closure page carry the specifics.

1.headline: January: ice on the park, elk in the meadows
1.body: The river is at its lowest and the rink at LaVern M. Johnson Park opens when a cold snap holds. Elk are down on the Hall Ranch and Heil Valley meadows, and the Nelson Loop can close for prescribed burns from mid-January. Rabbit Mountain dries first after each storm. Main Street is quiet and the kitchens are easy to get into.

2.headline: February: Old Man Winter, and a polar plunge
2.body: The mixed-terrain rally rides out of Bohn Park early in the month and the Polar Bear Club goes into the St. Vrain on Valentine's Day. South-facing trails are mud by noon and frozen by morning; go early or go to Rabbit Mountain. The rink runs in the cold spells.

3.headline: March: mud season, and the wind
3.body: The Lucky Lyons 5K and 10K, the first green on the meadows, and mud on everything that faces south. Rabbit Mountain is the reliable hike; Hall Ranch is trail-by-trail. The river starts to rise at the end of the month. Chinook winds can make the canyon mouth loud for days.

4.headline: April: Earth Day, first tents, first wildflowers
4.body: Tent camping opens mid-month at LaVern M. Johnson Park, the Ralph Price Reservoir fishing permits go on sale, and the first wildflowers show at Rabbit Mountain. The river climbs through the month and is not tubing water. The museum is still closed for the season; the galleries and the taprooms are not.

5.headline: May: runoff, and the town wakes up
5.body: The St. Vrain runs high, cold and brown with snowmelt: kayakers in the whitewater park, no tubes. Hall Ranch is dry and the wildflowers are at their best on the Nelson Loop. Campervan camping opens mid-month at the St. Vrain Trailhead. Memorial Day weekend is the first busy one; the Hall Ranch lot fills by nine.

6.headline: June: peak runoff, then the season starts
6.body: The river peaks in the first half of the month and drops toward tubing water by the end in a normal year; watch the gauge. The Lyons Outdoor Games fill Bohn Park and the whitewater park, the free concerts start in Sandstone Park, and afternoon storms begin: be off the ridge by one. Fire restrictions can start any time now.

7.headline: July: prime tubing, and RockyGrass
7.body: The classic float from the Apple Valley bridge through town, usually between 100 and 300 cfs. RockyGrass takes over the last full weekend and every bed with it. Concerts in the park, lightning by early afternoon on the trails, parking passes enforced in the park lots.
links: The festival weekend, without a car

8.headline: August: the Folks Festival, mellow water
8.body: The Rocky Mountain Folks Festival mid-month, then a quieter town. The river settles to mellow-to-prime tubing and the fishing turns on as it clears. Monsoon storms can close the Wapiti lot at Heil Valley Ranch; the Perseids are worth a late night at Rabbit Mountain.

9.headline: September: low water, best walking, elk bugling
9.body: The river is down to wading and fishing water, the days are clear and the nights cold. The artisan market in Bohn Park, the last concerts, and the elk bugling on the Hall Ranch meadows at dusk. Cottonwoods start to turn along the river at the end of the month. The best month for the trails.

10.headline: October: gold cottonwoods, the Spooktacular
10.body: The cottonwoods along the St. Vrain go gold in the first two weeks, the museum closes for the season, tent camping ends mid-month and the Halloween Spooktacular brings a costume parade down Main. Elk rut closures are possible on the county trails; the first snow sits on Longs Peak by month's end.

11.headline: November: quiet trails and a quiet town
11.body: Dry, sunny and empty. The lower trails at Hall Ranch and Rabbit Mountain are at their best between storms; Rabbit Mountain has hunting closures on some days, listed on the county page. The river is low and clear. Main Street puts its lights up after Thanksgiving.

12.headline: December: the Parade of Lights, then the rink
12.body: The holiday parade comes down Main Street early in the month with the tree lighting after it. The rink at LaVern M. Johnson Park opens with the first hard cold. Trails are dry between storms and the town's kitchens are yours on a weeknight.
